3. Several cards, several boxes and reports

AudiomothR version 0.4.0

Antonio Canepa-Oneto

Patricia de la Fuente Gamero

Source: vignettes/audiomothr-3-boxes.Rmd
audiomothr-3-boxes.Rmd

Abstract

How AudiomothR works with real monitoring: the successive cards of a box, a box moved between sites, coming back to the work another day, cards that were not copied, and PDF reports of one or several boxes.

This is the third of three vignettes of AudiomothR. The first one (vignette("audiomothr-1-workflow")) processed one card. In real work, an AudioMoth stays in the field for weeks or months: its SD card is replaced every few days, the box is sometimes moved to another site, the work is done over several days, and several boxes are compared. This vignette shows how AudiomothR handles all that.

library(AudiomothR)

One results folder per box

The key idea: each box (AudioMoth) has one results folder, given with output, and every card of that box is read into it. Each card becomes a deployment, with its own dates, site and location. All the steps (BirdNET, examples, validation, Observation.org, report) then work with all the cards of the box at once, each recording with the location of its own deployment.

~/AudiomothR_results/
├── box_01/      ← all the cards of the box FACADE0012345678
│   ├── AudioMoth_FACADE0012345678_deployments.csv   (one row per card)
│   ├── AudioMoth_FACADE0012345678_recordings.csv    (all the recordings)
│   ├── AudioMoth_FACADE0012345678_detections.csv    (all the detections)
│   └── recordings/  (copies of the cards, with copy_to = TRUE)
└── box_02/      ← all the cards of another box

Two different boxes cannot share a results folder (AudiomothR stops with an error if you try).

Two cards of the same box

To show it with the example card of the package, we split it into two “cards”, as if the SD card had been replaced between 7 and 15 October and the box had been moved about 4 km:

example_card <- system.file("extdata", "example", "card", package = "AudiomothR")
make_card <- function(day) {
  card <- file.path(tempdir(), paste0("card_", day))
  dir.create(file.path(card, day), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  file.copy(file.path(example_card, "CONFIG.TXT"), card)
  file.copy(list.files(file.path(example_card, day), full.names = TRUE), file.path(card, day))
  card
}
card_1 <- make_card("20261007")   # first card: 7 October
card_2 <- make_card("20261015")   # second card: 15 October

With real cards you do not need any of this: put the SD card in the computer and give its path.

The first card 

output <- file.path(tempdir(), "AudiomothR_results", "box_01")

am <- read_audiomoth(card_1, coordinates = "41.00, -3.00", site = "River - bridge",
                     output = output, copy_to = TRUE)
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpElCi7t/AudiomothR_results/box_01 is in the temporary folder of R: it
#>   is deleted when R closes.

Some days later: the next card

The second card is read with the same output. The box was moved, so its new coordinates and site are given:

am <- read_audiomoth(card_2, coordinates = "41.03, -2.97", site = "Pine forest",
                     output = output, copy_to = TRUE)
#> Copying the card to
#> /tmp/RtmpElCi7t/AudiomothR_results/box_01/recordings/20261015-20261015: 9 files
#> (2 MB).
#> ✔ Card copied (9 files): the analysis uses the copy, and the card can be
#>   formatted once you have checked it.
#> 
#> 
#> ── AudioMoth FACADE0012345678 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> • Card: /tmp/RtmpElCi7t/card_20261015 (copied)
#> 
#> • Copy of the card (used from now on):
#> /tmp/RtmpElCi7t/AudiomothR_results/box_01/recordings/20261015-20261015
#> 
#> • Site of this card: Pine forest (41.03, -2.97; ±698 m; source: argument)
#> 
#> • Deployments of this box: 2 (River - bridge, Pine forest)
#> 
#> • Map:
#> <https://www.openstreetmap.org/?mlat=41.03&mlon=-2.97#map=15/41.03/-2.97>
#> 
#> • Recordings: 16 in 2 days (2026-10-07 to 2026-10-15, Europe/Madrid time)
#> 
#> • Audio: 48,000 Hz, gain Medium, 0.7 min in total
#> 
#> • 10 with problems: duration < 3 s
#> 
#> • Battery: 4.9 V → 4.5 V
#> 
#> • Temperature: 11.7 to 34.4 °C
#> 
#> • Results in: /tmp/RtmpElCi7t/AudiomothR_results/box_01

The summary now says Deployments of this box: 2. The deployments are in am$deployments (and in AudioMoth_<ID>_deployments.csv):

am$deployments[, c("deployment", "site", "lat", "lon", "first_date", "last_date", "recordings")]
#>   deployment           site   lat   lon first_date  last_date recordings
#> 1  D20261007 River - bridge 41.00 -3.00 2026-10-07 2026-10-07          8
#> 2  D20261015    Pine forest 41.03 -2.97 2026-10-15 2026-10-15          8

and each recording knows its deployment and its location:

table(am$recordings$deployment, am$recordings$site)
#>            
#>             Pine forest River - bridge
#>   D20261007           0              8
#>   D20261015           8              0

What to know about the location of each card:

  • coordinates given: they are used (recommended).
  • Not given, and the card was already read before: the location it was given then.
  • Not given, new card: the location of its CONFIG.TXT (with a warning, since it is only right if it was updated in the AudioMoth app when the box was moved) or, if there is none, R asks for it in the console, where pressing Enter reuses the site of the previous card.
  • Reading the same card again replaces its deployment (it does not duplicate it); if new coordinates are given, its recordings are analysed again with the new location.

The copies of both cards are in recordings/, one folder per card:

list.files(file.path(output, "recordings"))
#> [1] "20261007-20261007" "20261015-20261015"

Analysing all the cards 

am <- analyze_birdnet(am)

analyze_birdnet() only analyses the recordings that have no result yet: after the first card, adding a card analyses only the new one. With the location filter, each card uses the species expected at its own site (vignette 2). Here, without BirdNET, we load the detections of the example card, as in vignette 1:

saved <- system.file("extdata", "example", "birdnet_detections.csv", package = "AudiomothR")
am$detections <- read_detections(saved)
file.copy(saved, file.path(output, "AudioMoth_FACADE0012345678_detections.csv"), overwrite = TRUE)
#> [1] TRUE

Everything else works with all the cards 

species_summary(am)
#>           scientific_name     common_name detections days recordings
#> 1       Motacilla cinerea    Gray Wagtail          1    1          1
#> 2            Cettia cetti Cetti's Warbler          1    1          1
#> 3 Troglodytes troglodytes   Eurasian Wren          1    1          1
#>   confidence_max confidence_mean location_prob example_candidates
#> 1         0.8222           0.822        0.2949                  0
#> 2         0.8196           0.820        0.5931                  0
#> 3         0.6319           0.632        0.2354                  0
obs <- export_observation(am, min_confidence = 0.5, min_detections = 1)
#> ✔ 3 records (3 species) for Observation.org in
#>   /tmp/RtmpElCi7t/AudiomothR_results/box_01/AudioMoth_FACADE0012345678_observation.csv.
#> ℹ Criteria: confidence ≥ 0.5, ≥ 1 detection per species and day.
obs[, c("date", "scientific name", "lat", "lng", "accuracy")]
#>         date         scientific name lat lng accuracy
#> 1 2026-10-07       Motacilla cinerea  41  -3      698
#> 2 2026-10-07            Cettia cetti  41  -3      698
#> 3 2026-10-07 Troglodytes troglodytes  41  -3      698

Each record of Observation.org takes the location of its own deployment: the detections of 7 October are at the bridge (41, -3); if there had been any on 15 October, they would be at the pine forest (41.03, -2.97). The examples, the validation page and the report also cover all the cards.

Coming back another day

The results folder keeps everything, so the work can stop at any time and go on another day (or on another computer, if the folder is in a shared or synchronised disk). To recover the am object, read the box again from its results folder: with copy_to, read the copy of a card (the card itself may have been formatted):

copies <- list.files(file.path(output, "recordings"), full.names = TRUE)
am <- read_audiomoth(copies[2], output = output)
#> 
#> ── AudioMoth FACADE0012345678 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> • Folder:
#> /tmp/RtmpElCi7t/AudiomothR_results/box_01/recordings/20261015-20261015
#> • Site of this card: Pine forest (41.03, -2.97; ±698 m; source: argument)
#> • Deployments of this box: 2 (River - bridge, Pine forest)
#> • Map:
#> <https://www.openstreetmap.org/?mlat=41.03&mlon=-2.97#map=15/41.03/-2.97>
#> • Recordings: 16 in 2 days (2026-10-07 to 2026-10-15, Europe/Madrid time)
#> • Audio: 48,000 Hz, gain Medium, 0.7 min in total
#> • 10 with problems: duration < 3 s
#> • Battery: 4.9 V → 4.5 V
#> • Temperature: 11.7 to 34.4 °C
#> • Results in: /tmp/RtmpElCi7t/AudiomothR_results/box_01

Nothing is copied or analysed again: the card was read before, so its deployment, site and location are kept (no coordinates needed), and the other deployments of the box are still there. The detections are read from the results folder:

am$detections <- read_detections(am)
nrow(am$detections)
#> [1] 6

With BirdNET, am <- analyze_birdnet(am) does the same and, if a recording was left without a result (an interrupted analysis), analyses it.

In an interactive session, output can even be left out: R suggests the folder used before for the same box (it remembers it by its device ID), and Enter accepts it (choose_output()):

am <- read_audiomoth(copies[2])
#> ℹ Results folder of this box (outside the card; it gathers all the cards of the box).
#>   Press Enter to use '/tmp/.../AudiomothR_results/box_01', or type another path.
#> Results folder:

When the card was not copied

Without copy_to, the inventory points to the files on the card. When the card is no longer connected (or has been formatted):

  • the results already obtained are kept, and the detections, the export to Observation.org and the report still work;
  • the steps that need the audio do not: analyze_birdnet() cannot analyse the recordings without a result (it warns card not connected), and extract_examples() and create_validation() cannot cut the clips.

Connecting the card again at the same path, or reading it again with read_audiomoth() wherever it is mounted, solves it. This is why copy_to is recommended.

The report of a box 

pdf <- create_report(am, title = "Monitoring of the river", open = FALSE)
basename(pdf)

(This block was not run when building the vignette: Quarto was not found on this computer.)

The report of a box covers all its deployments: the map shows both sites, and the tables of recordings and records state the site of each one.

Argument Meaning
recorders One box (am) or several (list(am1, am2))
by_recorder Several boxes: one section per box (TRUE, default) or all together (FALSE)
output Folder of the report (by default <output>/report/ of the box; required for several boxes)
title Title of the report
min_confidence Minimum confidence of the detections that count (0.5)
map Draw the map (needs maptiles, sf and terra for the background)
overwrite_template Replace a report.qmd edited by hand

Several boxes

Each box is read into its own folder, and create_report() takes a list of them:

river  <- read_audiomoth("E:/", coordinates = "41.123456, -3.123456",
                         output = "~/AudiomothR_results/box_01", copy_to = TRUE)
forest <- read_audiomoth("F:/", coordinates = "41.200000, -3.300000",
                         output = "~/AudiomothR_results/box_02", copy_to = TRUE)
river  <- analyze_birdnet(river)
forest <- analyze_birdnet(forest)

# One section per box
create_report(list(river, forest), output = "~/AudiomothR_results/report_2026")

# All the boxes together (a single summary of the species of the area)
create_report(list(river, forest), by_recorder = FALSE, output = "~/AudiomothR_results/report_2026_all")

In the report, each box is named after its site or, when it has been at several sites, after its device ID (AudioMoth FACADE0012345678); the map shows all the sites of all the boxes.

To process many cards in a script, process_audiomoth() can be used for each one (with Rscript, output must always be given):

cards <- c(box_01 = "/media/you/SD_01", box_02 = "/media/you/SD_02")
boxes <- lapply(names(cards), function(box) {
  process_audiomoth(cards[[box]], output = file.path("~/AudiomothR_results", box),
                    copy_to = TRUE, validation = TRUE)
})
create_report(boxes, output = "~/AudiomothR_results/report_2026")

Editing the report

create_report() writes a Quarto folder: report.qmd (the text and the code of the report), report_data.rds (the data), report_functions.R and the figures. You can edit report.qmd (e.g. add a paragraph about the study area or change a figure) and render it again, from a terminal in that folder:

quarto render report.qmd

or by calling create_report() again, which keeps your edits (unless overwrite_template = TRUE) and updates the data.

Summary

Situation What to do
New card of a box read_audiomoth(card, coordinates, output = <folder of the box>, copy_to = TRUE), then analyze_birdnet(am)
The box was moved The same, with the new coordinates and site
A location was wrong Read that card again with the right coordinates
Coming back another day read_audiomoth(<copy of a card>, output = <folder of the box>) and analyze_birdnet(am) or read_detections(am)
Another box Another output folder
A report of several boxes create_report(list(am1, am2), output = ...)

See also vignette("audiomothr-1-workflow") for the steps of one card and vignette("audiomothr-2-species") for the choice of species.
